supportedClaim: In this deterministic 2,500-file typed-array workspace harness, replacing per-file TextEncoder.encode(...).byteLength metadata construction with an allocation-free scalar UTF-8 byte counter preserved exact persistent metadata and report outputs while reducing the median metadata-only ArrayBuffer peak from 809,646 B to 27,500 B and the median 64-segment report ArrayBuffer peak from 808,449 B to 39,820 B, exactly matching the declared live runtime-body peak for that report fixture.
truthBoundary: This isolates TextEncoder-backed temporary typed-array allocation as the dominant ArrayBuffer construction peak in this fixture, not as a universal JavaScript memory rule.
It does not prove whole-process RSS equals the declared runtime-body peak.
It does not remove JavaScript heap/output-object memory.
RSS, heapUsed, and allocator behavior remain separate measurements.
Hosted timing medians are workload-specific observations, not universal speed claims.
The scalar UTF-8 counter is tested against representative Unicode and malformed surrogate cases but is not a standards-conformance proof over every possible JavaScript string.
nextEvidenceGate: Measure and attribute the remaining non-ArrayBuffer process/heap/output footprint now that typed-array backing-store peak has converged to the declared live-body peak.
